---
title: "Installing SeekDeep"
---

There are three ways to get SeekDeep. If you're going to run it through
[elucidatornf](running/elucidatornf.qmd) with Docker or Apptainer, you don't need to install it at
all: the workflows pull a container that already has it.

| | Best for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|
| [Conda / mamba](#conda) | Running SeekDeep commands directly | Linux x86-64, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| [Docker / Apptainer](#containers) | elucidatornf runs, clusters, Windows (through Docker Desktop or WSL2) | Anywhere Docker or Apptainer runs |
| [From source](#source) | Development, or platforms the packages don't cover | Linux, macOS |

## Conda / mamba {#conda}

SeekDeep ships in the `elucidator` package, together with
[elucidator](https://github.com/nickjhathaway/elucidator) and
[PathWeaver](https://github.com/bailey-lab/PathWeaver). It's published to its own channel on
prefix.dev, and the tools it calls (muscle, minimap2, bowtie2, bwa, samtools, BLAST and others)
come from conda-forge and bioconda.

```bash
mamba create -n seekdeep \
  -c https://prefix.dev/nickjhathaway/elucidator -c conda-forge -c bioconda \
  elucidator
mamba activate seekdeep
SeekDeep
```

`conda` works in place of `mamba` but is slower to solve. To update an existing environment:

```bash
mamba update -n seekdeep \
  -c https://prefix.dev/nickjhathaway/elucidator -c conda-forge -c bioconda \
  elucidator
```

## Docker / Apptainer {#containers}

The `nickjhathaway/elucidator` image has SeekDeep, elucidator, PathWeaver and the tools they call.
`develop` is the latest build, and every build is also tagged with its git commit, so pin a commit
tag for runs you need to reproduce.

```bash
docker pull nickjhathaway/elucidator:develop
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/data -w /data nickjhathaway/elucidator:develop SeekDeep
```

On a cluster with Apptainer (or Singularity):

```bash
apptainer pull elucidator.sif docker://nickjhathaway/elucidator:develop
apptainer exec elucidator.sif SeekDeep
```

elucidatornf picks the image itself: give it `-profile docker` or `-profile apptainer`.

## From source {#source}

You need a C++17 compiler (a recent clang or g++), `make`, `cmake`, `git`, Python 3 and
libcurl headers. `setup.py` downloads and builds the C++ libraries SeekDeep depends on into
`external/`, which takes a while the first time.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bailey-lab/SeekDeep.git
cd SeekDeep
./configure.py
./setup.py --compfile compfile.mk --outMakefile makefile-common.mk
make -j 4
```

`./configure.py` picks the compiler from `-CC`/`-CXX` if given, then from the `CC`/`CXX`
environment variables. Without either it uses `gcc`/`g++` on Linux (gcc 13 on Ubuntu 24.04, which
is what SeekDeep is tested with) and `clang`/`clang++` on macOS. To use a specific compiler:

```bash
./configure.py -CC gcc-13 -CXX g++-13
```

The binary ends up in `bin/SeekDeep`. Add that directory to your `PATH`, for example in
`~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/SeekDeep/bin:$PATH"
```

The `master` branch is the latest release and `develop` has the newest changes.

### Optional extras

Tab completion for SeekDeep's flags:

```bash
./setup.py --addBashCompletion
```

Some steps call external tools (muscle, BLAST, bowtie2 and others). A source build doesn't install
them, so install them yourself, for example from bioconda. The conda package and the container
already include them.

## Checking the install

`SeekDeep` with no arguments lists every command, and `SeekDeep <command> --help` prints a
command's flags. Commands and flags are not case sensitive.

```bash
SeekDeep
SeekDeep extractorPairedEnd --help
```

The same help text is in the [command reference](reference/index.qmd).
